title: Slow-cooker beef meatballs in tomato sauce
subtitle: Italian-style meatballs cooked slowly in a rich tomato sauce
excerpt: Beef meatballs cooked from raw in a simple tomato sauce until very tender. Serve over pasta or in rolls with lots of sauce.
sourceNotes: Meatballs in tomato sauce are central to Italian-American and southern Italian cooking. The slow-cooker method, where raw meatballs cook directly in the sauce, draws on the polpette tradition common across Italy.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight and reheat gently in a pan.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Better the next day. Make ahead and reheat gently; the meatballs absorb more sauce overnight.

content.text: The meatballs go into the slow cooker raw and cook directly in the sauce. This produces meatballs that are very moist and tender. They will not have a browned exterior, but after 5 hours in the sauce they become deeply flavoured all the way through. If you want a crust on the outside, brown them in a pan first.
Handle the meatball mixture as little as possible when forming. Overworking the mince makes them dense and tough. Wet your hands before rolling each one; the mixture will not stick to your palms.
Serve over spaghetti or pappardelle. Good with grated Parmesan and a little torn fresh basil.

Combine {{beef-mince}} of beef mince in a bowl with {{breadcrumbs-fresh}} of fresh breadcrumbs, {{eggs}} egg, {{parmesan}} of grated Parmesan, {{garlic-powder}} of garlic powder, and {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt. Mix briefly with your hands. Shape into balls about the size of a golf ball. You should get around 20 meatballs.

Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes, {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree, {{onion}} diced onion, {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, and {{bay-leaves}} of bay to the slow cooker. Stir briefly. Lower the meatballs gently into the sauce. Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 5 to 6 hours. The meatballs will cook through and be very tender. Discard the bay before serving.

rows.cause: The mixture did not have enough binding, or the meatballs were handled too roughly when placing in the sauce.
rows.fix: Stir the meat into the sauce and serve as a meaty tomato sauce. Next time add an extra egg or an extra tablespoon of fresh breadcrumbs.

rows.cause: The mixture was overworked when forming.
rows.fix: Nothing can be done now. Next time mix until just combined and handle as little as possible.

rows.cause: The meatballs released fat that diluted the sauce.
rows.fix: Set to HIGH with the lid off for 20 minutes. Or remove the meatballs and reduce the sauce separately.

rows.cause: No salt was added to the sauce, only to the meatballs.
rows.fix: Add a teaspoon of salt to the sauce, stir well, and cook for 10 more minutes. A pinch of sugar also helps tomato sauces that taste sharp.

content.text: Meatballs in tomato sauce appear across southern Italy as polpette al sugo. Italian immigrants brought the dish to America in the late 19th century, where it became central to Italian-American cooking. The slow cooker keeps the meatballs very moist; a hot oven or pan cannot do the same.
